questions.q: In a public cloud, who remains responsible for configuring access to the company's data?
options: No one; the cloud eliminates this risk
questions.explain: The provider secures the underlying infrastructure; the customer retains responsibility for their data, identities, and configurations.

questions.q: Which concept describes infrastructure defined in versioned files and deployed via a pipeline?
questions.explain: Infrastructure as Code (IaC): the desired state is defined in code; the risk is propagating a misconfigured template.

questions.q: Which criteria fall under business considerations in objective 3.1? (Select all that apply)
questions.explain: Data sovereignty, cost, ownership, and scalability are business criteria. Compute and power requirements are technical criteria.

questions.q: Match each model to its defining characteristic.

pairs.right: Infrastructure shared by a community of organizations
No Internet connection; transfers via controlled media

questions.explain: Each model shifts responsibility and the attack surface; the hybrid junction is often the weak point.

questions.q: Why should active vulnerability scanning be avoided on an industrial OT network?
options: Because OT systems never have vulnerabilities
Because it can disrupt equipment that controls physical processes
Because scans detect nothing on the network
questions.explain: In OT, availability and safety come first: an intrusive scan can halt a production line. Passive inspection is preferred.

questions.q: Which separation provides the strongest isolation but at the highest cost?
questions.explain: Physical segmentation (dedicated hardware and cabling) provides the strongest isolation, at the cost of expense and complexity.
